dimensions.reasoning: Review B successfully identifies several points also raised in Review A (e.g., infinite-sites proposal, quadrature approximation, microsatellite boundary truncation) but goes much further by identifying critical methodological gaps (unproven finite variance, lack of approximation bounds) and empirical confounders (asymmetric tuning, resampling). Its coverage of the most important issues significantly exceeds that of Review A, which focuses heavily on exposition.

While Review B does not rely on direct block quotes like Review A, it is highly precise in its references. It cites specific discussion contributions (Kuhner-Beerli Fig 9, Chen-Liu Fig 10), exact parameter values (θ=15), and specific theorems (Proposition 1(d)). It offers clear, actionable fixes.

Review B demonstrates exceptional technical engagement. Whereas Review A focuses frequently on notational inconsistencies and clarifications, Review B tackles the mathematical core of the paper (finite variance requirements for IS, approximation guarantees for the conditional sampling distribution) and rigorously questions the empirical evaluation design. This is a much deeper substantive engagement.

Review B flawlessly identifies rhetorical and methodological inconsistencies in the paper, particularly the authors' asymmetric treatment of the 'Fluctuate' method versus their own Q^SD regarding infinite variance and driving-value vulnerabilities. It accurately leverages the paper's own discussion section to ground these critiques.

strengths: Identifies fundamental theoretical gaps (finite variance, approximation bounds) that undermine the paper's empirical claims.
Leverages the published discussion contributions (Chen-Liu, Kuhner-Beerli) to expose confounders in the paper's efficiency comparisons.
Correctly points out rhetorical asymmetries in how the authors evaluate their own method versus competing methods.
weaknesses: Includes meta-commentary about AI agents ('Gemini claims...') in the Appendix concerns which distracts slightly from the core scientific review.
Misses some of the more detailed, albeit minor, notational ambiguities caught by Review A.
